IsolationForest.name: Isolation Forest
IsolationForest.simple: Imagine separating readings by asking a series of random questions about their values. An unusual reading often gets separated from the rest with fewer questions.
IsolationForest.technical: Isolation Forest builds randomized isolation trees. Shorter average path lengths are associated with observations that are easier to isolate.
IsolationForest.why: Provides a tree-based view of unusual combinations and can model nonlinear patterns without feature scaling in this project protocol.
IsolationForest.difference: It isolates observations through random partitions; LOF compares local density, while One-Class SVM learns a boundary around the training data.
IsolationForest.detects_well: Can surface points that are isolated in the feature space, including unusual combinations across weather variables.
IsolationForest.may_miss: May miss anomalies that are not easy to isolate, and behavior depends on the sampled trees and contamination setting.
IsolationForest.scaling: Unscaled input features in the existing model protocol.
IsolationForest.parameter_explanation: Contamination is the configured expected share of unusual training observations used to set the model's decision threshold. It is not measured sensor-fault prevalence or accuracy.

LocalOutlierFactor.name: Local Outlier Factor (LOF)
LocalOutlierFactor.simple: LOF compares a reading with its nearest neighbors. A point can look unusual when its local neighborhood is much denser than the area around that point.
LocalOutlierFactor.technical: LOF estimates local reachability density and scores observations relative to the density of their k-nearest neighborhoods. This project uses novelty mode for held-out observations.
LocalOutlierFactor.why: Adds a local-density perspective that can find observations unusual relative to nearby patterns even when the full dataset is varied.
LocalOutlierFactor.difference: LOF compares local densities; Isolation Forest isolates points globally through partitions, while One-Class SVM estimates a separating boundary.
LocalOutlierFactor.detects_well: Can identify locally isolated points when neighborhood structure is informative.
LocalOutlierFactor.may_miss: Results depend on the chosen neighborhood size and may be less informative when local density is unstable or the representation is poorly scaled.
LocalOutlierFactor.scaling: StandardScaler fitted to training rows only; transformed training and test rows are used.
LocalOutlierFactor.parameter_explanation: n_neighbors sets how many nearby training observations define the local comparison. The tested values are 10, 20, 30, and 50.

OneClassSVM.name: One-Class SVM
OneClassSVM.simple: It learns a flexible boundary around much of the training data. A new reading outside that learned region can be marked unusual.
OneClassSVM.technical: The RBF-kernel One-Class SVM estimates a support boundary in a kernel feature space. gamma='scale' controls the kernel's distance scale, and nu controls the boundary/allowed training outlier fraction constraints.
OneClassSVM.why: Provides a boundary-based perspective that differs from both isolation trees and local-density comparison.
OneClassSVM.difference: It separates the learned data region from the outside; Isolation Forest uses random isolation and LOF uses local neighborhood density.
OneClassSVM.detects_well: Can represent nonlinear boundaries around the scaled training distribution.
OneClassSVM.may_miss: Can be sensitive to nu, feature scaling, and the shape of the training distribution; an out-of-boundary point is not necessarily faulty.
OneClassSVM.scaling: StandardScaler fitted to training rows only; transformed training and test rows are used.
OneClassSVM.parameter_explanation: nu is a model control related to the upper bound on training errors and lower bound on support vectors. It is not a probability that a reading is faulty. RBF lets the boundary bend around nonlinear patterns.
